title: Distal right lower-lobe mucus plug — clinical diagram
styleNotes: Suitable for adolescents and adult learners
No blood or invasive procedural imagery
Do not use colour alone — hatch and dotted patterns plus labels
shows: Simplified front view of the lungs
Distal mucus plug in a right lower-lobe bronchial branch

altText.concise: Front-view lung diagram: open central airway via tracheostomy; distal mucus plug in right lower-lobe branch; reduced aeration beyond the plug; no pneumothorax.
altText.extended: Simplified front view of both lungs for an accessible medical simulation. A tracheostomy enters the central airway at the neck; the central airway is shown open and patent. A distal mucus plug sits in a right lower-lobe bronchial branch and is marked with a hatch pattern so it is not distinguished by colour alone. Lung tissue beyond the plug uses a dotted fill and a dashed outline to show reduced aeration. Labels state that suction through the tracheostomy may not reach a distal plug. The diagram explicitly notes that no pneumothorax is shown. Equipment and anatomy are schematic, without blood or procedural imagery.
